rv.q: Created by veterans of the revue "Beatlemania," this tribute show feeds off a seemingly endless appetite for all things Paul, John, George and Ringo. But after a show like this, the only impression that is left are those classic songs. And that's as it should be.
It hits all the right notes, but an imitation is still an imitation.

Consider it enhanced karaoke, like a collective night in front of a giant television playing the new Beatles video game, but without requiring the kind of hand-eye coordination and technological savvy so vexing to the middle-aged.

They're quite polished at what they do, which is to ape the Beatles' every intonation and gesture.

Aside from some cool-looking psychedelic scenery, Rain doesn't offer anything especially new. If you loved or hated 1977's Beatlemania, you already know your opinion of this show. (Indeed, all four cast members have performed in various iterations of that oft-revived revue.)
Your affinity for the Fab Four, cover-band mimicry and bad mop-top wigs will be a good gauge for whether or not this nonstop nostalgia trip is for you.
The homage often feels tired and cheesy, and audience members unwilling to frequently stand up and clap along may be uncomfortable.
That's surely a credit to The Beatles' songs, which have proven a lot more memorable — and, as Rain proves at its best, more theatrical — than most Broadway scores of late.
Just in time for Halloween comes “Rain,” the cheesiest slice of Beatles necrophilia since George Harrison’s doctor had him autograph a guitar as he lay dying of brain cancer.

cn.t: This well-traveled Beatles tribute show delivers faithful recreations of classic songs in an unambitious, somewhat cheesy concert format that will please die-hard fans but offers little beyond nostalgia.

vs.sum: The Neil Simon Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, although comfort is compromised by tight legroom and narrow seats. The ambiance is appealing with its classic architectural charm, and facilities are average, with typical restroom and concession offerings.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Step-free from street to Orchestra. No elevator.
